I couldn't verify any of the three pairs against the literature, so this is a judgment call based on structure.

- **Solution 2 (33, 47)** requires merging 75 rod groups into only 33 abstract types. Rod groups are extensions of Z by a finite point group, so their abstract type is largely fixed by the abstract point group and how it acts on Z. Many rod point groups are abstractly isomorphic, but I don't see how that would collapse the count by more than half.
- **Solution 3 (61, 68)** is structurally plausible but gives no mechanism for its specific counts.
- **Solution 1 (57, 63)** fits the structure best. Abstract isomorphism should only identify groups whose point groups are abstractly isomorphic and whose actions on the translation lattice match up to the extension. That gives a moderate reduction, consistent with the known fact that the 230 three-dimensional space groups reduce only to 219 abstract types (11 enantiomorphic pairs). The rod and layer reductions should be of similar modest size, which Solution 1 reflects.

I can't confirm the exact figures, so treat this as the most plausible of the three rather than a verified answer.

CHOICE: 1
